analysis.statement:
Patchboard manages reversible overlays on object attributes.

There are `N` objects and `K` permanently existing attribute cells. A cell stores either an integer (`I x`) or an object reference (`O x`).

A path consists of a root object and `L >= 1` attribute numbers. Starting at the root, read and follow the object reference in every attribute except the last; the last attribute identifies the target cell. Paths are resolved when used, against the current state.

Each activation now contains an ordered transaction of `M >= 1` replacements. On `START`, process its replacements from first to last. For each replacement, resolve its path after all preceding replacements in that same activation have been applied, remember the identified cell and its current value, then write the replacement value. After all replacements, append the activation ID to the global activation order. The ID is guaranteed inactive before `START`, but may be reused after stopping.

`STOP id` does nothing if `id` is inactive. Otherwise, restore that activation's remembered writes in reverse replacement order, then remove it from the global activation order. Each restoration writes the remembered value even if ano

plan.approach: Maintain a global map of defined cells keyed by (object,attribute). Each cell stores its current value (int or object ref). For each activation, keep a vector of (cell_key, old_value) in the order of replacements. The global activation stack holds activation IDs in order of activation. On START, resolve each replacement path sequentially using the current map, record the old value, write the new value, and push the activation ID onto the stack. On STOP, if active, pop the activation from the stack, then restore its recorded writes in reverse order, writing the remembered old value regardless of later changes. STOPALL repeatedly pops the newest activation and restores it until the stack is empty. GET resolves a path on the current map and outputs the cell’s value. STACK outputs the stack size and IDs from oldest to newest. All operations are O(total path length + total replacements).
data_structures: HashMap<u32, usize> id_to_index for quick active check
plan.complexity_target: O(total number of path steps + total number of replacements) ≈ O(6·10^5)
traps_to_handle: huge attribute numbers – use hash map, not array
path resolution must use current state after preceding replacements in same activation
remembered paths are never resolved again – store cell key directly
reverse restoration order – iterate writes vector backwards
STOPALL must restore each activation fully before next – pop from stack until empty
activation IDs may be reused – clear mapping on STOP
plan.return_shape: string of all output tokens separated by whitespace
test_ideas: Simple single START/STOP with one replacement and GET
Nested activations where inner overrides outer, then STOP inner and GET to see outer value
STOPALL after several activations, verify all restored
STACK after various operations, check order oldest→newest
Reusing an activation ID after STOP, ensure new activation works
Large attribute numbers (e.g., 10^9) in paths, ensure hash map handles them
Large integer values near 64‑bit limits, ensure no overflow
GET on a path that traverses multiple object references
STOP on inactive ID – no effect
STOPALL when no activations – no output
